Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through FinBot's inference workload. Really helpful conversation; below is a short recap so we have shared expectations and clear next steps.

TL;DR: primary goal is to bring down per-request inference costs while preserving response quality and keeping p95 latency under ~200ms for user-facing flows. You're open to quantization experiments but want to validate quality impact.

Key pain points you described
- Cost pressure: inference spend growing ~2.5x year-over-year; current unit economics are making expansion hard.
- Latency sensitivity: live chat and transaction flows need p95 < 200ms; some batch/analytics jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Inconsistent caching/batching: current stack doesn't have prefix/KV caching across requests, so redundant work is increasing tokens billed.
- Limited quantization testing: internal concerns about quality/regressions, so you need careful evaluation before production rollout.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Models: mix of open LLMs (Llama2-derived variants) served on AWS SageMaker endpoints
- Throughput: avg 8–12 QPS across peak pods, occasional spikes to ~60 QPS for product promos
- Payloads: prefix-heavy conversational history for auth/POV-preserving responses (sample attached)
- Ops: internal team manages endpoints and scaling; procurement prefers predictable pricing and clear savings projections

Success criteria (you mentioned)
- 2x+ reduction in inference TCO (per-user/session) or clear path to it within a POC
- Maintain conversational quality (no >5% drop in human evals)
- p95 latency <= 200ms for live flows at target QPS

Initial suggestions & how Redwood can help
- Batching + prefix/KV caching: for prefix-heavy workloads we typically see 30–60% cost reduction before any model compression.
- Quantization: 4-bit (Q4) or INT8-like execution can reduce inference cost 2–3x; we recommend an eval against your key prompts to quantify quality delta.
- Smart routing: route less-sensitive workloads to lower-cost variants or off-peak capacity to preserve budget and SLA.
- Technical POC: we suggest a 2-week POC: (1) ingest sample traffic, (2) run caching/batching config and quantization variants, (3) measure unit economics and quality on your prompts.

Attachments (sent):
- finbot-conversation-sample.json (sample payload you can use for eval)
- redwood-inference-cost-playbook.pdf (high-level playbook & expected gains)

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the primary procurement contact and timing? (you mentioned procurement@finbot.ai)
2) Please share 1–2 representative convo samples and a rough daily/monthly token estimate (attached sample looks good if you can confirm).
3) Ben (cc'd) — can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive next week to scope the POC?

Proposed times (PT): Tue 3/16 10–11am, Wed 3/17 2–3pm, Thu 3/18 9–10am — let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks again — excited to see if we can get you the savings you need without sacrificing quality.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great recap and aligned. A few clarifications / answers below: \n
- Procurement: yes, procurement@finbot.ai is the right distro (I copied Maya who owns infra procurement).
- Volume: roughly 25M tokens/day now; peak QPS hits ~60 for short bursts (as you noted).
- Quality: we care a lot about quality for user-facing chat — a 5% degradation on core intents is a non-starter. For non-user-facing flows (analytics, offline enrichment) we're flexible.
- Caching expectations: we'd expect a substantial win if prefix/KV caching can be applied to our conversational flows — curious what the realistic latency trade-offs are for cold starts.
- Quantization: we're open to testing 4-bit; main ask is a measurable A/B on key intents. If quality holds, we'd be supportive.

I've attached a sample payload from our prod logs. Ben/Maya — looping you in for any technical/contract items.

Thanks Alex — appreciate the details and the sample payload. Looping in Ben (Solutions Eng) and Neha (Sales Engineer) so we can scope the POC and the technical deep dive.

Short answers to your questions:
- Cold starts: we'll measure cold-start latency in the POC; with persistent KV cache warmup we typically get to target p95 within minutes for steady traffic. We'll include a short cold-start report in the POC deliverables.
- Expected savings (rough, subject to POC): caching/batching 30–60% for prefix-heavy requests; quantization 2–3x improvement in compute cost but we should validate quality on your intents. Combined, many customers reach ~3x effective cost reduction when both are applicable.
- Quality validation: we'll run a blind A/B on a held set of core intents and provide human/pass-fail summaries and token-level diff analysis.

Proposed immediate plan:
1) Technical deep dive (60m) — scope metrics we will capture, access you'll provide, and POC success criteria
2) POC (2 weeks) — ingest small slice of traffic, run caching/batching + quant variants, measure cost and quality
3) Final report & pricing recommendation — clear unit economics and recommended rollout plan

Proposed times (PT) for the deep dive: Wed 3/17 2–3pm, Thu 3/18 9–10am, Thu 3/18 3–4pm. Ben/Neha — which slot works?
